newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-WAUGH AND LAW POWER AUSTRALIA TO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH AND LAW POWER AUSTRALIA TO FINAL.

text.p: Half-centuries from Steve Waugh and Stuart Law propelled Australia to a three-wicket victory over India on Friday, and into the Singer World Series cricket final.
Auatralia will now play Sri Lanka in Saturday's final of the four-team limited overs tournament.
Waugh and Law took advantage of missed chances to thrust Australia to the brink of success with a fourth wicket stand of 113 as they pursued a target of 202 in 45 overs in the rain-hit match.
Waugh, dropped by Vinod Kambli at 34, went on to make 55 off 83 balls, hitting two fours. Having also taken one for 20, he won the man-of-the-match award.
Law struck a stylish 67 off 70 balls, including two sixes and three fours, after being dropped by Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar at 25.

After Waugh and Law were out in quick succession, Sri Lankan umpire K.T.Francis was the centre of controversy when India's fieldsmen challenged his decision to give Australian skipper Ian Healy not out on an appeal for run out.
Francis subsequently called for the third umpire to adjudicate on a slow motion television replay which showed Healy was in fact run out, having made four.
Healy and Michael Bevan, exchanged a few words with the umpire before Healy departed to some jeering from the crowd.
With four wickets left, Australia had to score five runs off the last over, bowled by leg-spinner Anil Kumble.
Brad Hogg was bowled for two off the first delivery but Paul Reiffel took a single off the next, giving the strike to Bevan, who struck the third ball through mid-on for four to clinch the win.
India, who were put in to bat, were dismissed for 201 in 41 overs after morning rain delayed the start by 85 minutes, reducing the game from 50 to 45 overs.
Indian wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia, promoted to open, provided a good start with 38 off 30 balls, hitting eight fours.
But wickets fell regularly, including Tendulkar for seven, so that India slumped to 89 for six in the 18th over.
Left-handers Saurav Gaguly and Sunil Joshi led a revival with a solid century stand off 20 overs.
Ganguly was top scorer with 59 off 75 balls, including seven fours, while Joshi struck five fours in his 48 from 67 deliveries.
Paceman Glen McGrath was the most impressive Australian bowler with three for 33 off nine overs.
